strategyPosture: Hold the current posture and let the dislocation screen do the work: the index is calm but narrow (SPY -0.5% from high, IWM -5.87% over 3m), credit is loose (SLOOS 0%, HY OAS 3.15%), and the actionable edge is in verified revenue-recovery names trading 28–69% below their highs — not in chasing the nuclear unwind. No new risk ahead of tomorrow's CPI with the 10-year already at 5.24%.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read is supported by credit, but breadth underneath is thin: IWM is -3.55% over 1m and -5.87% over 3m while SPY is +3.04% over 3m, so the calm is narrow, not broad. If lending standards tighten from 0% or HY OAS widens materially from 3.15%, the same Mag7 divergence stops being rotation and becomes the leading edge of a rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration state is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: the Mag7 average sits -8.97% from its 52-week high versus SPY at -0.5%, a -8.47-point divergence gap, with TSLA the weakest Mag7 name at -24.2% and AAPL strongest at -1.3%. Credit does not confirm stress — SLOOS lending standards are LOOSE at 0% (well below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is tight at 3.15%.
themes.label: Index calm, leadership rotating — not a rollover
themes.narrative: SPY at 777.87, just -0.5% from its 52-week high and +1.78% over the past month, reads as an all-clear: the market believes the index high means broad health.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS lending standards moving off 0% toward tightening, or HY OAS widening above 4% while the Mag7-to-SPY divergence gap stays beyond -8 points.

themes.counterRead: Equities are priced for the benign branch of tomorrow's CPI while the bond market is priced for the hot branch; both cannot be right. A hot print into a 5.24% 10-year leaves equities carrying the adjustment, because credit (HY OAS 3.15%) offers no cushion signal either way. A soft print, by contrast, would make the 5.60% 30-year the anomaly and steepen the case for duration-sensitive leaders.
themes.dataAnchor: The long end disagrees: DGS10 is 5.24%, DGS30 is 5.60%, the real 10-year is 2.91%, and the 2s10s curve is +0.49 — a bear-steepening profile, not a soft-landing one. Breakevens (T10YIE 2.33%) say this is term premium and real-rate pressure, not an inflation-expectations spiral. The CPI Sep 2026 print (Oct 14) is flagged HIGH signal strength in the event tracker, with headline expectations for a hot release already circulating.
themes.label: Long-end yields at cycle highs while equities price calm
themes.narrative: With VIX at 15.4 (down -9.94% over the past month) and SPY near highs, the equity market believes the rates story is settled and tomorrow's CPI is a formality.
themes.watchFor: Tomorrow's CPI print versus the hot-expectation headlines, and whether DGS10 holds above 5.2% or pushes toward 5.5% on the release.

themes.counterRead: Price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions in exactly the names with confirmed revenue recovery — that is the opportunity setup, not a value trap signal. The discipline is the screen's own caveat: the pullback posture is RESEARCH_SCREENED, meaning every candidate passed the 5-gate screen but the thesis still has to be verified name-by-name before sizing; a sentiment label is not itself evidence.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals say otherwise for the leaders of the screen. AVGO (a holding) is -28.3% from its high with revenue growing +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin, and a conviction score of 81 (Tier A) — the top-ranked name. APP is -63.3% from its high with revenue +55.8% YoY on the watchlist screen and RSI 33.2; NOW is -27.3% with revenue +23.1% YoY; NXT is -48% with revenue +31.6% YoY; KTOS is -68.9% with revenue +26.9% YoY. All five carry RECOVERY revenue inflections and were promoted on the watchlist this run.
themes.label: AI-infrastructure and software dislocations: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The tape treats the AI-infrastructure and enterprise-software complex as broken momentum: 24 tracked dislocations are flagged, most labeled SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, and the market believes the drawdowns are information.
themes.watchFor: Any of AVGO, APP, NOW, NXT, or KTOS losing its RECOVERY revenue inflection on the next earnings print, or RSI basing with a higher low while price stops making new drawdown lows.

themes.counterRead: This is the control case for the whole dislocation screen: where the decline has a confirmed fundamental cause, price and data agree and there is no gap to harvest. Treating TMDX as interchangeable with the sentiment-driven names would import exactly the error the screen exists to avoid — verify the decline reason before treating any single dislocation as opportunity.
themes.dataAnchor: The one high-materiality news item in the entire input contradicts the label: TMDX dipped after posting a Q1 earnings and revenue miss with falling margins (materiality score 8). Unlike AVGO or APP, there is no offsetting revenue-recovery figure in the conviction data for TMDX — it does not appear in top conviction or the watchlist promotions.
themes.label: TMDX: the dislocation screen's exception — this decline is fundamental
themes.narrative: TMDX screens like the rest of the dislocation list — -49.9% from its 52-week high, RSI 39.7, classified SENTIMENT_DRIVEN with a FULL_SIGNAL — implying the market has overshot on mood.
themes.watchFor: A subsequent TMDX print showing revenue growth re-accelerating and margins stabilizing, which would move it from fundamental decline to genuine dislocation.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is concentrated in the narrative-heavy, pre-profit names (SMR, OKLO) while the cash-generating incumbent (VST) holds a positive 1-month trend — the market is repricing story duration, not abandoning the power theme. Chasing the falling names here is catching the side where narrative was furthest ahead of data; the theme only becomes interesting again when the laggards stop making new 1-month lows on down days like today.
themes.dataAnchor: The 1-month laggard list is dominated by the complex: SMR -23.34% over 1m and -8.33% today, ASTS -17.96%, URA -13%, OKLO -12.74% over 1m and -8.92% today, CCJ -10.92%. The selling is accelerating into today, not stabilizing. Holding VST is -27.2% from its high but carries only a PARTIAL_SIGNAL, with a +6.6% 1-month trend — the profitable incumbent is diverging from the pre-revenue names.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI-power momentum unwind
themes.narrative: The nuclear and AI-power complex was priced as the purest AI-electricity trade; the market believed the story had years of runway without interruption.
themes.watchFor: SMR and OKLO posting a flat-to-positive day on a down tape, or VST losing its +6.6% 1-month trend and joining the laggards — the first signals stabilization, the second signals the unwind is spreading to quality.

watchFor: CPI Sep 2026 (Oct 14): hot versus soft print, and whether DGS10 holds above 5.2% or extends toward 5.5% afterward
HY OAS widening from 3.15% or SLOOS lending standards moving off 0% — either flips rotation into rollover risk
Mag7-to-SPY divergence gap: narrowing from -8.47 points confirms rotation; widening past -12 points with IWM still negative confirms narrow-market fragility
AVGO, APP, NOW, NXT, KTOS: revenue inflection staying at RECOVERY on next prints, and price basing rather than extending drawdowns
SMR/OKLO stabilization (a non-negative day on a down tape) versus VST losing its +6.6% 1-month trend
whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely materializes around tomorrow's CPI print colliding with a 5.24% 10-year and 5.60% 30-year: a hot print forces equities to do the adjusting the bond market has already done, while a soft print releases the most pressure exactly where dislocations are deepest (AVGO, APP, NOW). The FOMC decision on Oct 27–28 is the second trigger on the calendar.
